title: From AI concept art to a mobile game enemy — Beyond the Threshold
author: Intelligent-Bat-2370
selftext:
I'm developing Beyond the Threshold solo in Unity, with iOS as the first target. It's a stylized sci-fi action game with a ranged character, VAYA, and a katana fighter, VAEL.



This Sentry Drone board is AI-generated concept art, not a gameplay screenshot or a finished production model. The design direction is ivory armor, dark graphite machinery and a single orange eye. I've been exploring Tripo for the concept-to-3D step.



The practical challenge is keeping the design readable from a top-down camera on a phone. For this small enemy, my current target is around 2,000 triangles, one material and a 1K texture; those are starting targets, not measured performance results.



For others using AI concepts in a 3D pipeline: how do you keep the main silhouette consistent when moving from the reference image to a game-ready mesh? What tends to need the most manual cleanup?



The game is still in development. If the world interests you, I'll share progress and future playtest news on my profile.

replies.author: Intelligent-Bat-2370
replies.body: Thank you! Glad you like the direction. The orange eye against the ivory armor is the detail I want to keep readable when the drone is tiny on a phone screen.

replies.author: Tiny-Administration4
replies.body: I wish I could make something like that for my own (PC) game. Looking forward to what you're making!

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: One suggestion is to try having Codex or Claude do the re-meshing in Blender from the full high poly Tripo model. That way you can tell them your goal of preserving the top down view. I haven’t tried this specifically, but I had good success doing other re-meshing in Blender with Codex.

replies.author: Intelligent-Bat-2370
replies.body: Thanks for the suggestion! Checking the silhouette from the actual top-down camera makes sense. Have you found that workflow gives usable topology directly, or do you still need a manual retopology pass?

replies.author: SeasawPhilosopher
replies.body: Well I was doing realistic 3D rocks in meshy from concept art and when I re-meshed on meshy they looked bad even at 10k tris because it smoothed out the hard edges. So I had Codex import the full 1m+ tri mesh into blender and be smarter about preserving the relevant details and baking normals. The 500 tri mesh it did looked better than the 10k mesh from meshy!

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team. Really interesting seeing you frame the problem around mobile readability rather than just “does the model look good.”

The silhouette question is especially important for a top-down camera, since details that look great up close can disappear completely at gameplay distance.

Curious how much of the Tripo output you’re currently rebuilding or simplifying manually to get toward that \~2K triangle / one-material target. Is the bigger issue preserving the silhouette, or getting the generated mesh into the right technical budget?
